scope: Local synthetic data only. Browser checks were performed against the working source used to prepare this candidate, not a deployed website.

checks.method: Actual mouse calibration on the built-in invented drawing and six material-boundary points; actual export Blob contents captured, then built by the Python CLI and selected as mesh.json in the browser.

checks.detail: The download-event observer timed out after 10 seconds. The exported Blob payload was verified; filesystem save completion was not.

An initially selected file exposed metadata but File.text failed with NotReadableError. A byte-identical copy in a browser-readable temporary location loaded successfully. No filesystem or security permissions were changed.
Two parts loaded; all/individual selection, keyboard yaw and zoom, reset and mouse-drag orbit exercised. Keyboard zoom changed from 1 to 1.05.

checks.recovery: Valid image and mesh loaded after failures.

checks.detail: Default positive pitch showed the bowl cavity after view-depth correction. Linear-to-sRGB display mapping made dark illustrative surfaces readable. Built-in drawing labels were visible after fill-colour correction. This is not photorealistic material or shader-conformance certification.

At 390 by 844 CSS pixels, document width was 375 with no horizontal overflow and a single-column layout; part selection and keyboard zoom worked; observed WebGL error code was zero. Physical touch hardware was not tested.
Enter opened the numeric-alternative details; native part and range controls worked. Not a complete accessibility audit.
Local test instrumentation returned null for the viewer WebGL context and verified the fallback message. Instrumentation was removed and the page reloaded.
WEBGL_lose_context produced the expected context-loss message. Reload restored the viewer.
The window included same-origin fault-test script loading. This is not a claim about unobserved actions or other applications.
